manifest.title: Tree Nash Equilibria in the Network Creation Game

inputs.abstract:
In the network creation game, each player purchases incident undirected edges
at price $\alpha>0$ per edge and pays the sum of its distances to all players.
Disconnected pairs have infinite distance. A pure Nash equilibrium admits no
unilateral strategy change that reduces the changing player's cost.

This submission proves Theorem 3 of Fabrikant, Luthra, Maneva, Papadimitriou,
and Shenker, *On a Network Creation Game* (PODC 2003, p. 350): every tree Nash
equilibrium has social cost strictly less than five times the social optimum.
The optimum ranges over all strategy profiles, and the bound holds for every
positive edge price and every number of players at least two.

The concept package separates strategy profiles, individual cost, Nash
equilibrium, social cost, the inefficiency ratio, and the theorem statement.
The proof compares the distance savings obtained when both endpoints of a
tree path buy a link to its midpoint. The resulting distance bound, together
with unique edge ownership at equilibrium and a lower bound on every
profile's social cost, gives the strict factor-five inequality.

concepts.title: Inefficiency relative to the social optimum
concepts.description:
For fixed $n$ and edge price $\alpha$, the social optimum is the minimum
social cost over all strategy profiles. The inefficiency of a profile is
$\rho(s)=C(s)/\operatorname{OPT}(n,\alpha)$.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The optimum is encoded as an infimum. There are finitely many profiles and
the set of profiles is nonempty. For $n\ge2$, a connected profile exists and
every profile has social cost at least $n(n-1)>0$. Thus the infimum is an
attained finite minimum with a positive denominator in the theorem's domain.

The optimum ranges over all profiles, including networks with cycles. This
uses the actual social optimum for every edge price rather than prescribing
a star. The paper uses $\rho(G)$ for the ratio of an individual equilibrium;
the worst ratio over all equilibria is the price of anarchy.

namespace Lax899194.InefficiencyRatio

open Lax899194.NetworkCreationGame Lax899194.SocialCost
open scoped NNReal ENNReal

/-- The least social cost among all strategy profiles with `n` players. -/
noncomputable def optimalCost (n : ℕ) (α : ℝ≥0) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ⨅ s : Profile n, socialCost α s

/-- The social cost of a profile divided by the social optimum for the same game. -/
noncomputable def inefficiencyRatio {n : ℕ} (α : ℝ≥0) (s : Profile n) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  socialCost α s / optimalCost n α

end Lax899194.InefficiencyRatio

concepts.title: Pure Nash equilibrium
concepts.description:
A strategy profile is a pure Nash equilibrium when no player can reduce its
individual cost by changing its own strategy while all other players keep
their strategies. A deviation may replace the entire set of purchased edges.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
The comparison is between costs in the two resulting networks, including
deviations that disconnect the network. Equality is allowed, so weak and
transient equilibria are included.

The displayed equilibrium inequality on p. 348 of the paper has its direction
reversed. We use cost minimization, as specified by the surrounding discussion
and explicitly by footnote 4 on p. 350: the current cost is at most the cost
after any unilateral deviation.

/-!
---
title: Pure Nash equilibrium
type: definition
---
A strategy profile is a pure Nash equilibrium when no player can reduce its
individual cost by changing its own strategy while all other players keep
their strategies. A deviation may replace the entire set of purchased edges.

# Formalization notes

The comparison is between costs in the two resulting networks, including
deviations that disconnect the network. Equality is allowed, so weak and
transient equilibria are included.

The displayed equilibrium inequality on p. 348 of the paper has its direction
reversed. We use cost minimization, as specified by the surrounding discussion
and explicitly by footnote 4 on p. 350: the current cost is at most the cost
after any unilateral deviation.
-/

namespace Lax899194.NashEquilibrium

open Lax899194.NetworkCreationGame Lax899194.PlayerCost
open scoped NNReal

/-- No unilateral replacement of a player's strategy lowers that player's cost. -/
def IsNashEquilibrium {n : ℕ} (α : ℝ≥0) (s : Profile n) : Prop :=
  ∀ (i : Fin n) (t : Profile n),
    (∀ j : Fin n, j ≠ i → t j = s j) →
      playerCost α s i ≤ playerCost α t i

end Lax899194.NashEquilibrium

concepts.title: Network creation game
concepts.description:
There are $n$ players, indexed by $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. A strategy of player
$i$ is a set $s_i$ of other players: player $i$ purchases an edge to each member
of $s_i$. A strategy profile specifies one strategy for every player.

The resulting network $G[s]$ is undirected. Distinct players $i$ and $j$ are
adjacent when $j\in s_i$ or $i\in s_j$. Either endpoint may purchase an edge,
and both endpoints may purchase the same edge.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
Strategies are subsets of `Fin n`, with self-purchases excluded by their type.
Every such subset is finite. Edge ownership remains part of the profile even
though the resulting graph is a simple graph.

concepts.sourceText:
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Basic
import Mathlib.Data.Set.Card

/-!
---
title: Network creation game
type: definition
---
There are $n$ players, indexed by $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$. A strategy of player
$i$ is a set $s_i$ of other players: player $i$ purchases an edge to each member
of $s_i$. A strategy profile specifies one strategy for every player.

The resulting network $G[s]$ is undirected. Distinct players $i$ and $j$ are
adjacent when $j\in s_i$ or $i\in s_j$. Either endpoint may purchase an edge,
and both endpoints may purchase the same edge.

# Formalization notes

Strategies are subsets of `Fin n`, with self-purchases excluded by their type.
Every such subset is finite. Edge ownership remains part of the profile even
though the resulting graph is a simple graph.
-/

namespace Lax899194.NetworkCreationGame

/-- The other players to which player `i` purchases edges. -/
def Strategy (n : ℕ) (i : Fin n) := { S : Set (Fin n) // i ∉ S }

/-- A choice of strategy for every player. -/
abbrev Profile (n : ℕ) := (i : Fin n) → Strategy n i

/-- The undirected network formed by all purchased edges. -/
def graph {n : ℕ} (s : Profile n) : SimpleGraph (Fin n) where
  Adj i j := j ∈ (s i).val ∨ i ∈ (s j).val
  symm := ⟨fun _ _ h => h.elim Or.inr Or.inl⟩
  loopless := ⟨fun i h => h.elim (s i).property (s i).property⟩

end Lax899194.NetworkCreationGame

concepts.title: Individual cost in the network creation game
concepts.description:
For an edge price $\alpha>0$, player $i$ has cost
$c_i(s)=\alpha|s_i|+\sum_j d_{G[s]}(i,j)$.
The distance is the length of a shortest path, and is infinite if there is no
path. A player pays for every edge it purchases, including an edge also
purchased by its other endpoint.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
Costs take values in the extended nonnegative reals so that disconnected
networks retain the infinite penalty. `SimpleGraph.edist` supplies the graph
distance, and `ENat.toENNReal` preserves both finite distances and infinity.
The edge price is a finite nonnegative real; the theorem assumes it is positive.

/-!

title: Individual cost in the network creation game
type: definition
---
For an edge price $\alpha>0$, player $i$ has cost
$c_i(s)=\alpha|s_i|+\sum_j d_{G[s]}(i,j)$.
The distance is the length of a shortest path, and is infinite if there is no
path. A player pays for every edge it purchases, including an edge also
purchased by its other endpoint.

# Formalization notes

Costs take values in the extended nonnegative reals so that disconnected
networks retain the infinite penalty. `SimpleGraph.edist` supplies the graph
distance, and `ENat.toENNReal` preserves both finite distances and infinity.
The edge price is a finite nonnegative real; the theorem assumes it is positive.
-/

namespace Lax899194.PlayerCost

open Lax899194.NetworkCreationGame
open scoped BigOperators NNReal ENNReal

/-- Edge expenditure plus the sum of distances from player `i` to all players. -/
noncomputable def playerCost {n : ℕ} (α : ℝ≥0) (s : Profile n)
    (i : Fin n) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  (α : ℝ≥0∞) * (s i).val.ncard +
    ∑ j : Fin n, ((graph s).edist i j).toENNReal

end Lax899194.PlayerCost

concepts.title: Social cost
concepts.description:
The social cost of a strategy profile is the sum of all players' individual
costs: $C(s)=\sum_i c_i(s)$. Distances are counted over ordered pairs of
players. An edge purchased by both endpoints is charged twice.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
Social cost is defined on profiles so that it accounts for who purchases each
edge. The graph alone does not determine the expenditure when both endpoints
purchase an edge. No absence of double purchases is assumed in this definition.

namespace Lax899194.SocialCost

open Lax899194.NetworkCreationGame Lax899194.PlayerCost
open scoped BigOperators NNReal ENNReal

/-- The sum of all players' individual costs, with distances counted in both directions. -/
noncomputable def socialCost {n : ℕ} (α : ℝ≥0) (s : Profile n) : ℝ≥0∞ :=
  ∑ i : Fin n, playerCost α s i

end Lax899194.SocialCost

concepts.title: Tree Nash equilibria have inefficiency below five
concepts.description:
For every positive edge price $\alpha$ and every tree Nash equilibrium $T$,
$\rho(T)<5$: its social cost is strictly less than five times the social
optimum.

sections.title: Formalization notes
sections.markdown:
There are at least two players, making the cost ratio well-defined with a
positive denominator. `SimpleGraph.IsTree` means connected and acyclic.
The equilibrium is a strategy profile whose resulting undirected network is
a tree; the profile retains edge ownership and the costs of deviations.
No non-transience assumption or lower bound such as $\alpha\ge2$ is imposed.

sections.title: Reference
sections.markdown:
Theorem 3, p. 350, in Fabrikant, Luthra, Maneva, Papadimitriou, and Shenker,
[*On a Network Creation Game*](https://people.eecs.berkeley.edu/~kubitron/courses/cs294-4-F03/papers/p347-fabrikant.pdf),
PODC 2003, pp. 347-351, DOI: 10.1145/872035.872088.

import Lax899194.NashEquilibrium
import Lax899194.InefficiencyRatio
import Mathlib.Combinatorics.SimpleGraph.Acyclic

/-!
---
title: Tree Nash equilibria have inefficiency below five
type: theorem
---
For every positive edge price $\alpha$ and every tree Nash equilibrium $T$,
$\rho(T)<5$: its social cost is strictly less than five times the social
optimum.

# Formalization notes

There are at least two players, making the cost ratio well-defined with a
positive denominator. `SimpleGraph.IsTree` means connected and acyclic.
The equilibrium is a strategy profile whose resulting undirected network is
a tree; the profile retains edge ownership and the costs of deviations.
No non-transience assumption or lower bound such as $\alpha\ge2$ is imposed.

# Reference

Theorem 3, p. 350, in Fabrikant, Luthra, Maneva, Papadimitriou, and Shenker,
[*On a Network Creation Game*](https://people.eecs.berkeley.edu/~kubitron/courses/cs294-4-F03/papers/p347-fabrikant.pdf),
PODC 2003, pp. 347-351, DOI: 10.1145/872035.872088.
-/

namespace Lax899194.TreeNashEfficiency

open Lax899194.NetworkCreationGame Lax899194.NashEquilibrium
open Lax899194.InefficiencyRatio
open scoped NNReal

/-- Theorem 3: every tree Nash equilibrium has inefficiency strictly below five. -/
axiom statement (n : ℕ) (hn : 2 ≤ n) (α : ℝ≥0) (hα : 0 < α)
    (s : Profile n) (hNash : IsNashEquilibrium α s) (hTree : (graph s).IsTree) :
    inefficiencyRatio α s < 5

end Lax899194.TreeNashEfficiency

statements.signature:
statement : ∀ (n : Nat),
  instLENat.le 2 n →
    ∀ (α : NNReal),
      NNReal.instPartialOrder.lt 0 α →
        ∀ (s : Lax899194.NetworkCreationGame.Profile n),
          Lax899194.NashEquilibrium.IsNashEquilibrium α s →
            (Lax899194.NetworkCreationGame.graph s).IsTree →
              ENNReal.instPartialOrder.lt (Lax899194.InefficiencyRatio.inefficiencyRatio α s) 5
statements.doc: Theorem 3: every tree Nash equilibrium has inefficiency strictly below five.

proofs.description: Every tree Nash equilibrium has inefficiency strictly below five.

sections.title: Proof strategy
sections.markdown:
For a path of length $D$, let $r$ be its integer midpoint. Every vertex lies
beyond $r$ from at least one endpoint. If both endpoints buy a link to $r$,
their combined distance savings are at least $n(\lfloor D/2\rfloor-1)$.
The two Nash inequalities bound this by $2\alpha$, giving
$D\le 3+4\alpha/n$.

Positive edge price rules out duplicate purchases at equilibrium. A tree
therefore has $n-1$ purchases, and its social cost is at most
$5\alpha(n-1)+3n(n-1)$. Every connected profile has social cost at least
$\alpha(n-1)+n(n-1)$; disconnected profiles have infinite cost. Since
$n\ge2$, the former upper bound is strictly less than five times the latter
lower bound. The optimum is positive and finite, so division proves the claim.

sections.title: Attribution
sections.markdown:
The conclusion is Theorem 3 of Fabrikant, Luthra, Maneva, Papadimitriou,
and Shenker, *On a Network Creation Game* (PODC 2003, p. 350).
This proof uses a midpoint argument instead of the paper's centroid argument.
Tree paths, distances, and finite edge counting use mathlib.
